 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

 Shri Mohammad Baseem Khan - Advocate for the appellant.

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri Ravindra Singh Kushwaha - Deputy Advocate General for the
respondent-State.

Heard on I.A. No.6477 of 2024, first application under Section 389(1) Cr.P.C. for suspension of
sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the appellant - Salman Ali who has been convicted
under Section 363 of Ipc and sentenced to undergo 02 years Ri with fine of Rs.1000/-, Section 366
of Ipc and sentenced to undergo 03 years' Ri with fine of Rs.1000/- and Section 376(3) of Ipc and
sentenced to undergo 21 years' Ri with fine of Rs.3000/- with default stipulations respectively vide
judgment of conviction and order of sentenced dated 06-12-2019 passed by Second Additional
Sessions Judge, Shivpuri in Special Case No.83/2018.

Prosecution story as found proved is that the present appellant has abducted the prosecutrix (PW-2)
who was minor at that time and committed rape upon her.
Prosecutrix in her statements has fully supported the story of prosecution.

The prosecution has also established its case and the age of the prosecutrix by calling the scholar register of the prosecutrix alongwith Vijay Kumar Tiwari (PW-6)
who was Head Master of the school.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that it is a case of consent and prosecutrix had gone with the appellant on motorcyle on her own volition and lived with him.
Appellant has already suffered incarceration of 05 years and 04 months.
Hence, appellant prays for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
Learned counsel for the respondent-State opposed the prayer on the ground that at the time of incident, prosecutrix was minor, therefore, consent, if any, shall have no consequence.

So far as age of the prosecutrix is concerned, the same has duly been proved by the prosecution by producing scholar register and prosecutrix in para 6 of her cross-examination has given explanation that in which manner she was taken by the appellant and rape was committed upon her.

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid, we are not inclined to grant suspension of sentence and bail to the appellant.
Hence, I.A. No.6477 of 2024 is rejected.

At this stage, learned counsel for the appellant submits while convicting the appellant, the trial Court has relied upon the DNA report but the same has not been exhibited in the trial and it was not confronted with the accused during his statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
For the purpose of exhibiting the DNA report in the record, matter is remitted back to the IInd Additional Sessions Judge, Shivpuri.
Let the record of this case be sent back to the trial Court.

The trial Court is directed to call the appellant/ accused from the concerned jail as well as the prosecution for exhibiting the DNA report in the record.
 (VIVEK RUSIA) (RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI)
 JUDGE JUDGE  vc VARSHA CHATURVEDI
